title: Robust Signal Enhancement via Fractional Detail Views and Knowledge Guided Multi-view Fusion
one_liner: FracKGMF enhances very noisy signals by widening local time-frequency interactions and weighting each view by an estimated reliability score before fusion.
lead: When the signal-to-noise ratio is very low, each time-frequency bin becomes unreliable. Standard enhancement systems often inspect only a short local neighborhood and then make a hard suppression decision from evidence that may already be corrupted. FracKGMF changes both parts of that process. Its FracConv layer gathers weak cues from a longer-tailed neighborhood, and its fusion module uses a Wiener-style reliability estimate so uncertain regions are not treated as equally trustworthy as clean ones. The result is a system that suppresses noise without erasing as much faint signal structure.

paras: Signal enhancement on a time-frequency map is hard at low SNR because the local evidence is corrupted exactly where the model must decide what to keep and what to remove. A short-time Fourier transform gives a grid over time and frequency, but a single cell in that grid may contain a faint signal, strong noise, or both.

Many enhancement models rely on ordinary convolution (a local weighted filter) over that grid. That works when nearby cells remain informative. Under heavy corruption, however, a short neighborhood can be dominated by noise. The model then suppresses too much, leaving speech gaps or signal distortion, or suppresses too little, leaving residual artifacts.

callout.b: The core issue is not just missing capacity.
callout.html: The model is often confident in the wrong time-frequency regions because it treats noisy local evidence as trustworthy.

steps.b: Convert the signal to a time-frequency representation
steps.text: Build the enhancement problem on a grid where each cell stores local energy over time and frequency.
Process the grid with FracConv so each cell can receive information from both nearby and farther cells with distance-dependent weights.
Use a Wiener-inspired score to estimate which regions are likely to carry trustworthy signal evidence.

steps.b: Fuse the views with that reliability score
steps.text: Weight contributions from each view according to reliability instead of averaging them blindly.
Map the cleaned time-frequency estimate back to the signal domain.

paras: FracKGMF changes both the neighborhood model and the fusion rule. It replaces a fixed short-range local filter with fractional distance decay interactions, and it replaces plain multi-view fusion with reliability-aware fusion guided by a score derived from classical Wiener reasoning.
object.object: time-frequency interaction pattern plus reliability-aware fusion rule

hidden.name: How trustworthy each time-frequency region is
paras: The decisive variable is not raw energy. It is reliability: does the evidence in this region look more like stable signal structure or random corruption? A bright patch in a spectrogram may still be noise, while a faint patch may be a real harmonic or pulse that repeats consistently across nearby context.

FracKGMF estimates reliability with a Wiener-inspired score. The score does not solve the enhancement problem by itself. Instead, it calibrates the fusion stage, so views extracted from uncertain regions are downweighted and views from more trustworthy regions carry more influence.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark regions where the model should trust the evidence more during fusion.

reads.html: Reliability says whether the local evidence deserves influence. The method works better when uncertain regions are treated cautiously rather than confidently suppressed, because heavy noise can make a local peak look real when it is only corruption.
The Wiener-inspired reliability score calibrates multi-view fusion, so heavy corruption does not push the network toward excessive suppression in ambiguous time-frequency regions.

mechanism.h2: Why long-tailed neighborhoods and reliability-guided fusion fit this problem
paras: FracConv matters because a faint signal pattern may not be identifiable from one small neighborhood. Weak but consistent evidence can be spread across a broader region. A fractional distance decay weighting rule still favors nearby cells, but it does not cut off farther cells sharply. That gives the model access to longer-range consistency without making every cell influence every other cell equally.

The fusion rule matters because different views are not equally trustworthy under heavy noise. If one view says a region has strong signal while the reliability score says the region is unstable, then that view should not dominate the decision. KGMF uses the score as a gate on fusion, so confidence is tempered where the evidence is weak.

These two pieces address different failure modes. FracConv improves evidence gathering, because it lets weak structure accumulate across distance. KGMF improves decision making, because it converts that gathered evidence into a conservative or assertive fusion weight depending on reliability. The combination therefore changes both what the model sees and how much it trusts what it sees.

stages.s: Extract long-tailed local interactions with FracConv
Estimate reliability score for each region
Enhanced signal with fewer missed weak components

math.words: A cell receives contributions from nearby and farther cells, but the weight decays smoothly with distance instead of dropping to zero outside a short window.
math.equation: y_i = sum_j w(d(i,j)) x_j where w(d) falls as distance grows
symbols: input value at neighboring time-frequency cell j
output value at target cell i
distance between the target cell and source cell
distance-decay weight used by the fractional interaction family

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose the target cell is ambiguous and its nearest three neighbors each carry weak evidence with values 0.2, 0.2, and 0.1.
A short local filter may stop there and produce a small response.
FracConv also reads farther cells with values 0.15 and 0.12, but downweights them because they are farther away.
If the near weights are 1.0, 0.8, 0.6 and the farther weights are 0.3 and 0.2, the output becomes 0.2 + 0.16 + 0.06 + 0.045 + 0.024 = 0.489.
That larger pooled signal matters because the weak pattern is now visible enough to survive the later fusion decision.

math.note: The method does not trust distant cells equally. It keeps them in play with smaller weights so weak structure can accumulate without flooding the target cell.

charts.title: Fixed-resolution local enhancement
charts.note: The model can act decisively, but the decisions are often based on unreliable local evidence.

charts.title: FracKGMF
charts.note: The abstract reports especially large gains at extreme noise, including a 33 dB average improvement on one EM benchmark at -20 dB.

items.html: If the reliability score marks real weak signal as unreliable, the fusion stage will downweight the very evidence the system should keep, because the gate treats that region as unsafe.
If the decay is too slow, distant noise can contaminate the target cell, because the model gathers context from too broad a neighborhood.
If the chosen analysis window blurs short events or narrow spectral lines, later enhancement cannot fully restore what the front end already smeared.
The method works best when the decay pattern is broad enough to gather consistent weak cues and the reliability score separates stable structure from corruption with reasonable accuracy.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Create a benchmark with paired clean and noisy signals at several SNR levels, including an extremely low setting. Compare three models: a standard local enhancement network, the same network with FracConv only, and the full FracKGMF system. Plot time-frequency maps before and after enhancement, along with a per-region reliability estimate. The demo should show whether weak repeated structure is retained rather than wiped out.
demo.closing: The key evidence is not only the final score. It is that the full system keeps weak structure in ambiguous regions because it gathers broader evidence and uses reliability to moderate fusion.
